label: US citizenship / lawful-presence status
questionText: Are you a US citizen, a lawful permanent resident (green card), or here on a temporary visa?
inferenceHints: Customer mentions passport/naturalization/citizenship certificate → us-citizen. Green card / I-551 → permanent-resident. Visa / I-94 / EAD → temporary-lawful-presence. FLHSMV requires lawful presence for every DL/CDL issuance.

valueLabels.temporary-lawful-presence: Temporary visa or other non-immigrant status (work, student, etc.)

label: Primary identity document available
questionText: Which primary identity document do you have? A US passport, certified birth certificate, certificate of naturalization, certificate of citizenship, or consular report of birth abroad?
inferenceHints: Customer names any of those documents. 'My license' is NOT a primary identity document for REAL ID. Copies are not accepted for any of these; originals only.

label: Social Security card available (original, not copy)
questionText: Do you have your original Social Security card with you? Copies are not accepted.
inferenceHints: 'I have my SSN memorized' is NOT yes. 'I have a copy / photo' → yes-copy-only, which will not be accepted. Non-citizens without work authorization may have 'not-issued'.

valueLabels.yes-copy-only: I only have a copy / photo

label: Number of St. Lucie County residential-address proof documents available
questionText: How many proofs of your St. Lucie County residential address can you bring? Examples: utility bill, bank statement, lease, deed, voter registration card.
inferenceHints: FLHSMV requires TWO. One from List A (deed/mortgage/lease/utility/bank/voter reg) and one from List B. If customer has none but is a minor or new resident, the parent's documents or Declaration of Domicile can substitute — flag for clerk.

label: Name has changed since primary ID was issued
questionText: Has your legal name changed since your primary identity document (passport/birth cert) was issued? If yes, do you have the certified name-change document (marriage cert, divorce decree, court order)?
inferenceHints: Church-issued marriage certificates are NOT accepted. Customer must also have updated SSA 24-48h before visit.

valueLabels.yes-with-docs: Yes — I have the legal documents
valueLabels.yes-missing-docs: Yes — but I don't have the documents

label: Current FL license is not REAL ID compliant and customer wants upgrade
questionText: Does your current Florida license have a gold star in the upper corner (REAL ID compliant)?
inferenceHints: Gold star = already-compliant, no REAL ID docs required for renewal. No gold star + customer wants federal ID acceptance → needs-upgrade. New residents always need-upgrade.

valueLabels.already-compliant: Yes — gold star already on my license
valueLabels.needs-upgrade: No gold star, I want to upgrade
valueLabels.declining-upgrade: No gold star, and I'll skip the upgrade
valueLabels.na-no-fl-license: I don't have a Florida license

label: Active-duty military service member
questionText: Are you currently on active-duty military service, or a veteran?
inferenceHints: Active duty affects title transfer (military orders accepted in lieu of address proofs), sales-tax exemption on vehicles brought into FL under orders, and fee waivers under §322.21(8). Veteran-not-active qualifies for fee waivers but not active-duty rules.

label: Origin of prior license / residency
questionText: Where are you moving to Florida from? Another US state, a US territory, or another country?
inferenceHints: Foreign-country applicants often require additional translation or foreign-license verification and cannot use NLETS. US territories (PR, USVI, Guam, AS, MP) count for REAL ID primary ID acceptance.

label: New Florida resident within 30 days
questionText: Have you recently moved to Florida (within the last 30 days or planning to stay)?
inferenceHints: FL statute requires DL transfer within 30 days of establishing residency. 'I just moved here' / 'I'm new to Florida' → yes.

label: Out-of-state / out-of-country driver license status
questionText: Is your out-of-state driver license currently valid? Do you have it with you?
inferenceHints: We must verify via NLETS. If not in NLETS and expired, customer needs a Certified Driving Record from prior state. Expired >1yr from a non-NLETS state often requires re-testing.

valueLabels.valid-in-nlets: Valid — but not with me (in NLETS)

label: Lawful-presence documents available (non-citizen path)
questionText: Do you have your lawful-presence documents with you (green card, EAD, visa + I-94)?
inferenceHints: For temporary lawful presence, the DL expiration is tied to the I-94 / visa expiration. Required for every non-citizen issuance.

valueLabels.no: No, I don't have them with me

label: Condition of the original title document
questionText: Does the title have any whiteouts, line-throughs, scratch-outs, or missing signatures?
inferenceHints: ANY alteration on the face of the title is rejected — customer must obtain a corrected title from seller. Missing seller sig → seller must come in or sign and return. Missing purchaser name on the 'seller must enter purchaser's line' → bill of sale required. na-no-title is an auto-resolved sentinel set when title_possession is electronic-held or lost-or-none — there is no physical title to inspect, so this question is skipped.

valueLabels.na-no-title: N/A — no paper title to inspect

label: Title comes from out of state / out of country
questionText: Is the vehicle currently titled in Florida or in another state/country?
inferenceHints: OOS titles add VIN verification (HSMV 82042 or Section 7 of 82040), out-of-state registration copy, and title-holding-state rules.

label: Physical status of the out-of-state title
questionText: Do you have the original paper title, a photocopy, or is your state an electronic-title state?
inferenceHints: Photocopies are never accepted. Title-holding states with electronic titles require the OOS writing packet (we write to lienholder). Non-title-holding states without paper title → look up the state's title-law per cartitles.com reference. na-fl-title is auto-resolved for Florida titles; na-no-title is auto-resolved when title_possession is electronic-held or lost-or-none (no paper title to classify).

label: How registered owners are joined on the title
questionText: Is there more than one name on the title? If so, are the names joined by AND or by OR?
inferenceHints: Joined-and: every owner must sign (or POA). Joined-or: any one owner may sign. Matters for both title transfer and duplicate title.

label: Vehicle has an active lien or is leased
questionText: Does the vehicle have a lien, or is it leased?
inferenceHints: Lien-active: lienholder letterhead letter with VIN/make/year OR copy of OOS title showing lien. Lease: lease agreement + lessor letter authorizing FL 'registration-only'.

label: Age status of the person taking title
questionText: Is the person whose name will be on the title 18 or older?
inferenceHints: Per FL statute, minor purchasers require an adult co-purchaser on title. Confirm the co-purchaser is at least 18 and will be present to sign.

label: How long the customer has owned the vehicle
questionText: How long have you owned this vehicle?
inferenceHints: Less-than-6-months triggers FL 6% Use Tax + local option tax unless out-of-state sales tax proof is presented. Foreign-country imports always owe full 6% + local regardless of duration.

label: Sales tax already paid in another state
questionText: Did you pay sales tax when you bought this vehicle in the other state? Do you have the bill of sale or purchase agreement showing the tax paid?
inferenceHints: Only matters if ownership_duration is less-than-6-months. Without proof, FL collects the full 6% FL Use Tax.

label: Where the vehicle is being imported from
questionText: Was this vehicle previously titled in Florida, in another US state, or imported from another country?
inferenceHints: Foreign-country: full 6% FL Use Tax + local option tax always due, regardless of ownership duration. VIN verification on FL-imported foreign vehicles often needs customs documentation.

label: Who will hold title
questionText: Will the title be in an individual's name, a business name, or a trust?
inferenceHints: Business: Sunbiz active-registration printout required, registered-agent verification. Trust: certification-of-trust or trust agreement; multiple trustees means all must come in or provide POA.

label: Current Florida PDL + PIP insurance with company + policy#
questionText: Do you have current Florida auto insurance? We need the insurance company name and policy number.
inferenceHints: No FL insurance → we can perform title work ONLY, no registration. Out-of-state insurance is not acceptable for registration.

label: Odometer disclosure status
questionText: Does the title have a completed odometer disclosure, or do you have a bill of sale showing the mileage?
inferenceHints: If vehicle is model-year 2010 or older → exempt (federal). 2011+ requires disclosure. If odometer on title is less than previously recorded → flag as 'NOT ACTUAL'. na-inheritance is an auto-resolved sentinel for deceased-owner transfers: the deceased can't sign a seller's odometer disclosure, so the standard bill-of-sale odometer item does not apply (SME-confirmed) and this question is skipped.

valueLabels.yes-bill-of-sale: Yes — on a bill of sale

label: Vehicle model year range (odometer rules)
questionText: What year is the vehicle?
inferenceHints: 2010-or-older vehicles are exempt from federal odometer disclosure. 2011-or-newer requires mileage disclosure at transfer. na-odometer-moot is an auto-resolved sentinel used only when the odometer disclosure itself is moot (e.g. an inheritance transfer): the model year is asked solely to gate the odometer item, so when that item can't apply the year question is skipped.

label: Vehicle is physically present at the office for VIN verification
questionText: Will you be bringing the vehicle to the office so we can do the VIN verification?
inferenceHints: Only relevant for OOS titles. Yes → deputy performs VIN verification on-site. No → VIN verification must be done by law enforcement ahead of the visit; customer brings completed HSMV 82042 or Section 7 of 82040. na-fl-title is an auto-resolved sentinel (set when title_is_oos=no-florida): a vehicle already on a Florida title needs no VIN verification, so the question is skipped.

label: Someone else is signing the title application on the owner's behalf
questionText: Will the person whose name is going on the title be present at the appointment, or will someone else be signing on their behalf?
inferenceHints: Absent owner requires notarized POA document with original signature or DocuSigned POA. POA must be submitted with the title work that goes to the state.

label: CDL expiration status
questionText: Is your CDL currently valid? If expired, how long has it been expired?
inferenceHints: More-than-1-year: FL cannot renew — treat as original CDL (re-test all knowledge and skills exams). Less-than-1-year: renewable but late fee applies. Expiration drives the dominant branch for CDL work.

label: Which CDL flow applies
questionText: Are you renewing an existing Florida CDL, transferring a CDL from another state, applying for a brand-new CDL, or upgrading from a CLP?
inferenceHints: Each origin has different document + test requirements. oos-transfer requires valid out-of-state CDL; fl-original-first-time requires General Knowledge exam passed; fl-clp-upgrade requires CLP held 2+ weeks before skills exam.

valueLabels.fl-original-first-time: Brand new — never had a CDL
valueLabels.fl-clp-upgrade: Upgrading my CLP to a CDL

label: Out-of-state CDL is currently valid
questionText: Is the CDL from your previous state currently valid?
inferenceHints: Invalid OOS CDL → re-test all written and skills exams, or customer can return to origin state to renew first.

label: Customer wants hazmat endorsement this visit
questionText: Do you need a hazmat endorsement on your CDL?
inferenceHints: Hazmat requires TSA background check ($91) + $7 per endorsement + $75 CDL app fee. Hazmat test valid only 60 days. Must be taken in English, no audio form. Walton office does NOT have a hazmat machine.

label: Customer has funds for TSA background check fee
questionText: Have you paid the TSA background check fee ($91) for the hazmat endorsement?
inferenceHints: Without TSA fee paid, customer must return. Only asked if has_hazmat_endorsement_request is yes.

label: Customer is required by law to carry a CDL medical card
questionText: Are you required by law to carry a CDL medical examiner's certificate (DOT physical card)?
inferenceHints: Excepted intrastate drivers are not required. Most interstate drivers are. This controls whether medical_cert_in_system is needed.

label: Current medical card uploaded to FL system
questionText: Has your medical examiner's certificate been uploaded to the Florida system by your physician's office?
inferenceHints: If no and recently updated, customer contacts the physician's office to upload. We cannot accept paper cards in place of the system record. Only applies when medical_cert_required=yes.

label: CDL General Knowledge exam status
questionText: Have you passed the CDL General Knowledge written exam? If yes, can we verify it in ADLTS?
inferenceHints: passed-not-in-adlts → customer must obtain certified driving record showing exam was passed. not-passed → schedule/offer testing.

label: Age of the most recent passed CDL General Knowledge exam
questionText: When did you pass the CDL General Knowledge exam?
inferenceHints: More-than-1yr since passing → must re-test all written and skills exams.

label: CDL skills exam status
questionText: Have you passed the CDL skills (driving) exam?
inferenceHints: Skills exam cannot be taken until 2 weeks after CLP issuance. If not-passed but eligible, offer scheduling.

label: Time elapsed since CLP issuance
questionText: When was your Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) issued?
inferenceHints: Less-than-2-weeks: skills exam not yet eligible. 2-weeks-or-more: eligible.

label: Applicant is a school employee
questionText: Are you a school district employee applying for a school-bus endorsement?
inferenceHints: School employees must present school employment ID card or letter from the school department on every original and renewal. CDL customers generally cannot use the Address Certification Form — school employees are the exception per vendor workflow.

label: Applicant can communicate in English (for CDL exams)
questionText: Can you read and communicate in English?
inferenceHints: Effective Feb 6 2026, all FL DL exams are English-only. CDL General Knowledge exam must be passed in English and may not be taken in audio form. Hazmat retest may be in English or Spanish and may use audio.

label: Applicant wears corrective lenses for driving
questionText: Do you wear glasses or contacts to drive? If yes, do you have them with you today?
inferenceHints: Yes-not-with-me → customer cannot take vision test today; must return with corrective lenses or visit eye doctor. Failure of vision test → form DL 10 referral.

valueLabels.yes-with-me: Yes — and I have them with me
valueLabels.yes-not-with-me: Yes — but they're not with me

label: Applicant is at least 17.5 years old (CDL testing age floor)
questionText: Are you at least 17 years and 6 months old?
inferenceHints: CDL test requires age 17.5+. Federal interstate CDL requires 21+; intrastate FL allows 18+. This fact gates testing eligibility.

label: How the customer wants to renew their driver license
questionText: Would you like to renew online at MyDMV Portal, or do you need to come in-office?
inferenceHints: Online renewal available every other renewal cycle per FLHSMV. In-office required if customer used online last renewal, holds a CDL, needs a photo update, is changing name/designation, or is getting their first FL credential.

label: Whether the customer's current FL credential is REAL ID compliant (gold star)
questionText: Does your current Florida driver license or ID card have a gold star in the upper right corner (REAL ID compliant)?
inferenceHints: FLHSMV began issuing REAL ID compliant credentials in January 2010. Non-REAL-ID customers need the full REAL ID document set on this visit.

label: Whether the customer has changed Florida residential address since their last credential
questionText: Has your Florida residential address changed since your current license or ID was issued?
inferenceHints: Florida law requires address update within 30 days of a move. Combining the renewal with an address change is supported on the same in-office visit.

label: Whether the customer wants the Veteran (V) designation added to the credential
questionText: Would you like the 'Veteran' designation added to your Florida driver license or ID card?
inferenceHints: Veteran designation requires DD-214 (honorable discharge) or VA veteran ID card. One-time designation; once added, carries forward through renewals. If the customer says they aren't a veteran, record not-a-veteran — this also implies is_100_percent_disabled_veteran=no so the disability follow-up is skipped.

label: Whether the customer has a VA-documented 100% total and permanent service-connected disability
questionText: Do you have a VA letter showing a 100% total and permanent service-connected disability rating?
inferenceHints: Per §322.21(1), 100% T&P disabled veterans qualify for a no-fee Florida driver license, ID card, or CDL. Requires VA letter showing the 100% T&P rating.

label: Which certified name-change document the customer has
questionText: Which document certifies your name change — a marriage certificate, divorce decree, or a court order?
inferenceHints: FLHSMV accepts only certified/original documents from the issuing clerk of court. Hospital marriage certificates, religious ceremonies, or uncertified copies are not accepted.

label: Whether the customer has already updated their name with the Social Security Administration
questionText: Have you already updated your name with the Social Security Administration?
inferenceHints: FLHSMV cross-checks the name-on-credential against the SSA record as part of REAL ID verification. If SSA has not been updated, the credential change will fail at submission; customer must visit SSA first.

label: Which ID-card scenario applies
questionText: Are you applying for your first Florida ID card, downgrading from a driver license, replacing a lost/stolen card, or upgrading to REAL ID?
inferenceHints: Downgrade from DL typically happens when an 80+ customer fails the vision exam. Replacement is eligible for MyDMV online. REAL ID upgrade requires the full document set.

valueLabels.downgrade-from-dl: Downgrade my license to an ID

label: Applicant's age bracket (drives parental-consent + online-exam rules)
questionText: Are you (or the applicant) under 18 or 18 or older?
inferenceHints: Under 18: parental consent required; online knowledge exam available via approved third-party providers. 18+: in-person or third-party knowledge exam; no parental consent required.

label: Whether the applicant has completed the TLSAE/DETS course required for first-time licensees
questionText: Have you completed the Traffic Law & Substance Abuse Education (TLSAE) course — also called DETS for minors? It's required before applying for a learner's license for first-time licensees.
inferenceHints: TLSAE/DETS is only required for applicants who have never held a driver license in any state or country. Completion is reported electronically to FLHSMV by approved providers.

valueLabels.na-previously-licensed: Held a license before — not required

label: How the applicant will take (or took) the Class E Knowledge Exam
questionText: Will you take the Class E Knowledge Exam in-office, online through an approved third-party provider, have you already passed it, or did you complete it through a high school DELAP program?
inferenceHints: Online exams are only available to applicants under 18. In-office is available to any age. DELAP is high-school-specific. Exam is 50 questions, 80% required to pass, English only.

label: Whether a parent or legal guardian (over 18) is physically at the office to sign for a minor applicant
questionText: Will a parent or legal guardian over age 18 be present to sign for the minor at the office?
inferenceHints: Must be a legal parent or guardian — siblings and adult-non-guardians don't qualify. Parent must bring a valid government-issued photo ID.

valueLabels.yes: Yes — a parent/guardian will be there

label: Whether the vehicle being renewed has a gross vehicle weight of 55,000 lbs or more (triggers HVUT)
questionText: Does the vehicle have a gross vehicle weight (GVW) of 55,000 lbs or more?
inferenceHints: Heavy Vehicle Use Tax applies at 55,000 lbs GVW or more. Customer must present IRS Form 2290 or proof of exemption.

label: Whether the customer qualifies for the Initial Registration Fee exemption under §320.072
questionText: Are you acquiring this vehicle from an immediate family member at the same address, through inheritance as a surviving spouse, or using existing license-plate credit in your name?
inferenceHints: Per §320.072, immediate-family transfers (same residential address), surviving-spouse inheritance, and plate-credit transfers all exempt the $225 Initial Registration Fee. HSMV 82002 documents the exemption.

label: Which plate the customer wants to use for the new registration
questionText: Do you want a new standard Florida plate, transfer an existing plate registered to you, or get a specialty/personalized plate?
inferenceHints: Transferring an existing plate avoids the Initial Registration Fee. Specialty plates add an annual surcharge on top of the standard registration.

label: Whether the customer is applying for a Disabled Veteran license plate
questionText: Are you applying for a Disabled Veteran (DV) license plate?
inferenceHints: Requires VA Summary of Benefits letter specifying 100% service-connected OR 100%-compensation-rate OR DVA-financed vehicle. Per §322.21, one plate is fee-reduced; additional DV plates pay standard fee.

label: Why the tag or decal needs to be replaced
questionText: Why does the plate or decal need to be replaced — was it stolen, never arrived in the mail, or is it damaged/defaced?
inferenceHints: Stolen requires police report or case number. Lost-in-transit within 20 days of an online renewal is free; after 20 days, standard replacement fees apply.

label: Whether replacing the metal plate or just the annual decal
questionText: Are you replacing the metal license plate, the annual decal, or both?
inferenceHints: Decal-only replacement has a lower fee than full plate replacement. HSMV 83146 works for either.

label: Who is surrendering the license plate and their relationship to the registration
questionText: Is this plate in a personal name (yours or someone else's) or a business name, and are you the registered owner/agent?
inferenceHints: Third-party surrender requires either LPSA signed by owner or HSMV 82053 POA. Business surrender by non-agent requires agent-signed letter or POA.

label: Whether someone other than the registered owner is signing
questionText: Are you the registered owner of this plate, or are you surrendering it on someone else's behalf?
inferenceHints: Third-party signing requires either LPSA signed by owner in advance OR notarized POA.

label: Which specialty-plate scenario applies
questionText: Are you putting a specialty plate on your vehicle now, buying a pre-sale voucher for yourself, or buying a voucher as a gift for someone else?
inferenceHints: Pre-sale vouchers exist for plates that haven't reached the FLHSMV issuance threshold yet. Once threshold met, voucher holders get the plate issued.

valueLabels.new-plate-on-existing-vehicle: New plate on a vehicle I already own
valueLabels.voucher-gift: Buying a voucher as a gift

label: Whether the customer has eligibility proof for the specialty plate they want
questionText: Does your chosen specialty plate require eligibility documentation (university affiliation, professional license, etc.), and do you have it?
inferenceHints: Many specialty plates gate on membership or credential status. If eligibility is required but not presented, BLOCK until it is.

label: Whether the specialty-plate voucher is for the customer or someone else
questionText: Is the voucher for yourself or a gift for someone else?
inferenceHints: Gift vouchers require the recipient's name + license plate number or driver license number at time of transaction.

label: Whether the customer wants to process the duplicate title online, by mail, or in-office
questionText: Would you like to process the duplicate title online via MyDMV Portal, by mail, or in-office?
inferenceHints: Online option only works for electronic titles with no lien. Online fee $4.50, mail fee $2.50, in-office fees on FLHSMV schedule.

label: Current holding status of the title
questionText: Is your title currently held electronically by the state, is it a paper title you have in hand, or is it a paper title you've lost?
inferenceHints: Electronic-held + no-lien → online conversion eligible. Lost-paper → HSMV 82101 duplicate. Paper-in-hand shouldn't be in duplicate-title flow.

label: Where the customer purchased the new vehicle
questionText: Did you purchase this vehicle from a franchise dealer, from a private seller in Florida, from a private seller out-of-state, or did you inherit it?
inferenceHints: Franchise dealers typically process title + tax directly. Private OOS purchases require VIN verification and bill of sale.

label: Which parking-placard scenario applies
questionText: Are you applying for an original placard, renewing an existing one, or replacing a lost/damaged placard?
inferenceHints: Replacement uses HSMV 83146. Renewal also requires a new HSMV 83039 signed within the last 12 months plus a copy of the expiring placard's registration.

label: Type of parking-placard applicant
questionText: Is the applicant an individual Florida resident, an out-of-state resident, an out-of-country visitor, or an organization/business?
inferenceHints: Out-of-state visitors with an ISA-marked home-state placard are honored automatically (no FL permit needed). Otherwise visitors get a $15 temporary placard. Organizations complete the Application by an Organization section on HSMV 83039 and identify themselves with an FEID or FL sales-tax registration number.

label: How old the physician's HSMV 83039 certification is
questionText: Was your HSMV 83039 certification dated within the last 12 months?
inferenceHints: Certifications older than 12 months are not accepted; customer must obtain a new one from a qualifying medical professional.

label: Permanent vs. temporary placard
questionText: Is this for a permanent placard (4 years, no fee) or a temporary one (no more than 6 months, $15)?
inferenceHints: Permanent placards are blue and free. Temporary placards are red, expire on a date the physician sets (≤6 months), and cost $15. Statute §320.0848(1)(a) waives the temporary fee if a second temp is issued within 12 months of the first.

label: Qualifying medical condition certified on HSMV 83039
questionText: Which qualifying condition has your physician certified on HSMV 83039 (boxes 2–8)?
inferenceHints: FLHSMV requires the certifier to check at least one of seven qualifying conditions on HSMV 83039. Optometrists may sign only for legally-blind. If none of these conditions apply, the application will be rejected at the office — ask up front to save the trip.

valueLabels.severe-arthritic-neuro-orthopedic: Severe arthritic, neurological, or orthopedic limitation

label: Type of medical professional signing HSMV 83039
questionText: Who is signing the medical certification on HSMV 83039?
inferenceHints: Per §320.0848(1)(b)2 and HSMV-Main: Florida-licensed physician, osteopath, physician assistant, chiropractor, podiatrist, optometrist (sight conditions only), or APRN. Out-of-state physicians must include a separate signed statement showing they understand FL eligibility rules. VA Form Letter 27-333 substitutes for HSMV 83039 medical certification — but only at renewal or replacement, not initial.

label: Reason for replacement (when scenario=replacement)
questionText: Why are you replacing the placard?
inferenceHints: Per §320.0848(2)(d): replacements cost $1, except $0 when stolen with a police report or lost-in-transit within 180 days of issuance. The 'na-not-replacement' value is auto-set by fact-implications when scenario != replacement.

valueLabels.lost-in-transit: Lost in transit (within 180 days of issuance)

label: Police report for stolen placard
questionText: Do you have a police report listing the stolen placard?
inferenceHints: Statute §320.0848(2)(d) waives the $1 replacement fee when a stolen placard is reported and the police report accompanies the application. The 'na-not-stolen' value is auto-set by fact-implications when replacement_reason != stolen.

label: Special Exception (homebound) path needed
questionText: Are you applying because the disability is too severe to come into a tax-collector or DL office in person to obtain a Florida driver license or ID?
inferenceHints: F-83039 page 1 has a Special Exception line the certifying physician signs to waive the FL DL/ID requirement for severely disabled permanent applicants. F-83039 wording restricts this to permanent applicants. Without this, no FL DL/ID = blocked.

valueLabels.yes: Yes — physician will sign Special Exception

label: Visitor has an ISA-marked home placard
questionText: Do you already have a parking placard or plate from your home state or country that shows the international wheelchair symbol?
inferenceHints: Per HSMV-Vis and §316.1958, Florida honors home-state and home-country placards that display the international symbol of accessibility. No Florida permit is needed in that case. The 'na-not-visitor' value is auto-set when applicant_type is FL or organization.

valueLabels.yes: Yes — home placard shows the wheelchair symbol

label: Prior temporary placard issued within last 12 months
questionText: Have you been issued a temporary placard in the last 12 months?
inferenceHints: Per §320.0848(1)(a) and F-83039 §3a, a second temporary placard issued within 12 months of the first is free; outside that window the $15 fee applies again. Auto-set to 'na-not-temporary' when duration != temporary.

label: Eligible for an additional secondary permit
questionText: Are you eligible for an additional permit because you are a frequent traveler (plane / train / bus / vessel) or a quadriplegic?
inferenceHints: Per §320.0848(2)(c), an individual may hold up to two permits only if they are a frequent traveler or a quadriplegic. The secondary permit expires on the same date as the primary, regardless of issuance date. Not available for temporary permits.

valueLabels.none: Not applying for an additional permit

label: Organization identifier type
questionText: What identifier will the organization provide to be affixed to the permit — an FEID or a Florida sales-tax registration number?
inferenceHints: Per HSMV-Org: organizations must provide one of FEID or FL sales-tax registration number. Sunbiz registration is NOT an accepted identifier (the prior tree referenced it; corrected). Auto-set to 'na-not-organization' when applicant_type != organization.

label: Whether disabled person or a guardian signs
questionText: Will the disabled person sign the application themselves, or will a parent or guardian sign on their behalf?
inferenceHints: F-83039 signature line allows either the disabled person or their guardian to sign. §320.0848(1)(c)3.b explicitly authorizes the applicant or the applicant's parent or guardian.

valueLabels.parent-or-guardian-signs: Parent or guardian signs on their behalf

label: Visitor origin (US state vs. foreign country)
questionText: Are you visiting from another US state or from a foreign country?
inferenceHints: Out-of-country visitors may submit a copy of their home-country parking permit in lieu of an HSMV 83039 medical certification. Auto-set to 'na-not-visitor' when applicant_type is FL or organization.

label: Origin of the vessel being registered
questionText: Where is the vessel from — Florida already, another US state, a foreign country, antique (30+ years), or a non-titled vessel?
inferenceHints: Antique (30+ years) has a special registration. Non-titled vessels use HSMV 87244. OOS vessels require title surrender.

label: Vessel length in feet
questionText: What is the length of the vessel in feet?
inferenceHints: Vessel length determines registration class and fee.

label: Vessel propulsion type
questionText: Is the vessel motorized, a sailboat, or purely oar/paddle-powered?
inferenceHints: Non-motorized small vessels may be exempt from titling (not registration).

label: What the customer wants to do with the vessel registration
questionText: Are you titling and registering the vessel for the first time, just renewing registration, transferring to a new owner, or getting a duplicate?
inferenceHints: Registration-only flow doesn't need the title-application form.

label: Whether the applicant currently holds an active FL learner's license
questionText: Do you currently hold a valid Florida learner's license?
inferenceHints: A valid learner's license is a prerequisite for the Class E Driving Skills Test.

label: Which St. Lucie County office is hosting the road test
questionText: Which office will you be doing the road test at — Walton, Tradition, or Ft. Pierce?
inferenceHints: Each office has its own parking/route guide. Walton and Ft. Pierce do most tests; Tradition has limited availability.

label: Which property-tax transaction applies
questionText: Are you making a standard payment, setting up installments, making a partial payment, updating your mailing address, or asking about exemptions?
inferenceHints: Exemption inquiries go to the Property Appraiser, not the Tax Collector. Installment plan requires DR-534 by April 30.

label: Whether the property-tax payment is delinquent
questionText: Are you paying current-year taxes or delinquent taxes?
inferenceHints: Delinquent payments require guaranteed funds only (no personal checks). Interest accrues per §197.252.

label: Whether the customer is the property owner
questionText: Are you the owner of the property?
inferenceHints: Installment plan and partial payment applications require owner signature. Standard current-year payments can be made by anyone.

label: How the customer wants to pay
questionText: How will you be paying — cash, personal check, cashier's check, debit, or credit?
inferenceHints: Personal checks NOT accepted for delinquent taxes.

label: Where the mobile home was purchased
questionText: Did you purchase the mobile home from a Florida dealer, an out-of-state dealer, a private seller, or did you inherit it?
inferenceHints: Florida dealers are legally required to process the title. OOS-dealer + private-seller flows require customer to submit HSMV 82040 at the tax collector.

label: Whether the customer owns the land the mobile home sits on
questionText: Do you also own the land the mobile home sits on?
inferenceHints: Yes → eligible for RP decal (permanent, $5.10) AND title retirement. No → standard annual mobile-home decal applies.

label: Whether the customer is transferring a decal from a previously owned mobile home
questionText: Are you transferring a decal from a mobile home you previously owned?
inferenceHints: Decal transfer avoids a new decal fee; customer must bring the current registration and decal number.

label: Current status of the mobile home title with respect to retirement
questionText: Has the mobile home's title already been retired to real property?
inferenceHints: Already-retired means future transfers use a deed, not an HSMV title application — no action at the tax collector.

label: Whether the customer has already filed the retirement paperwork with the Clerk of the Circuit Court
questionText: Have you already filed the title-retirement paperwork with the St. Lucie County Clerk of the Circuit Court?
inferenceHints: Clerk filing must happen BEFORE tax collector filing. Clerk has their own fees.

label: Whether the customer is applying for a new CCW license or renewing an existing one
questionText: Is this a new concealed-weapon license or a renewal of an existing one?
inferenceHints: Renewals do not require new firearms-training documentation; new applications do.

label: Applicant's age bracket for CCW eligibility
questionText: How old is the applicant?
inferenceHints: Florida CCW minimum is age 21. Exception: servicemembers (§250.01) and honorably-discharged veterans qualify at 18+. Under 18 never qualifies.

label: Whether the applicant has a firearms-training certificate
questionText: Do you have a firearms-training certificate (NRA, hunter safety, law-enforcement course, or state-certified instructor)?
inferenceHints: Active-duty military and honorably-discharged veterans can substitute military orders or DD-214 for a training certificate.

label: Whether the applicant has any disqualifying condition from §790.06
questionText: Do you have any felony convictions, domestic-violence injunctions, two or more DUIs within the last 3 years, mental-health adjudications, dishonorable discharge, or controlled-substance issues that might affect eligibility?
inferenceHints: Any yes or unsure should route the customer to review the Application Instructions PDF and contact FDACS before scheduling. Rights-restored felons may still qualify.

label: Which FWC recreational-license category the customer needs
questionText: Which license do you need — hunting, saltwater fishing, freshwater fishing, or a combo?
inferenceHints: Combos (Sportsman, Gold Sportsman) bundle hunting + fishing + common permits.

label: Whether the applicant is a Florida resident
questionText: Are you a Florida resident?
inferenceHints: Residents pay lower fees, qualify for lifetime licenses, and access certain exemptions. Non-residents buy visitor-duration licenses.

label: Applicant's age bracket for FWC license purposes
questionText: How old is the applicant?
inferenceHints: Under-16 and 65+ residents are exempt from license fees per §379.353.

label: How long the customer wants the license to last
questionText: How long should the license last — annual, 5-year, or lifetime? (Non-residents can also buy short-term 3-day or 7-day.)
inferenceHints: Lifetime licenses require Florida residency.

label: Whether the applicant qualifies for the Military Gold Sportsman's License
questionText: Are you a Florida resident currently on active-duty US military?
inferenceHints: Active-duty Florida-resident servicemembers qualify for the reduced-rate Military Gold Sportsman's license.

label: Which §379.353 exemption category applies (if any)
questionText: Do you qualify for a license-fee exemption (senior 65+, under 16, disabled FL resident, armed forces home on leave, hunting/fishing on your homestead)?
inferenceHints: Exemptions waive the fee entirely; customer still needs to bring the appropriate proof (age, DL, disability cert, military orders).

label: What the customer wants to do with their Business Tax Receipt
questionText: Are you applying for a new Business Tax Receipt, renewing an existing one, modifying it, or closing your business?
inferenceHints: New and renewal both involve payment; modify routes to Tax Specialist email; close uses the Business Tax Closure form.

label: Jurisdiction where the business is located
questionText: Which jurisdiction is your business located in — unincorporated St. Lucie County, City of Port St. Lucie, City of Fort Pierce, or St. Lucie Village?
inferenceHints: City-limits businesses need BOTH a city BTR and a county BTR. Unincorporated businesses only need the county BTR but must complete county zoning first.

label: Whether the business uses a name other than the owner's legal name
questionText: Is your business using a name other than your own legal first and last name (a DBA, fictitious name, or business entity name)?
inferenceHints: Fictitious names require SunBiz registration (Florida Division of Corporations) before the BTR can issue.

valueLabels.no-own-legal-name: No — using my own legal name

label: Broad category of the business (drives special pre-requirements)
questionText: What kind of business is this — a general business, a state-regulated profession, a pest-control business, or a lawn/landscape business using fertilizers or pesticides?
inferenceHints: Regulated-profession businesses need state professional license first. Pest-control and lawn/landscape need FDACS certification.

label: Whether a state professional license is required and already held
questionText: If your occupation is regulated by a state agency, do you already hold the state-issued license?
inferenceHints: State license must be obtained BEFORE the BTR application.

label: Whether unincorporated-area zoning approval has been completed
questionText: Have you completed the St. Lucie County Zoning process (required only for unincorporated-area businesses)?
inferenceHints: Unincorporated-area businesses must complete zoning BEFORE applying for BTR. City-limits businesses don't use this process.

label: Whether the business requires a county fire inspection
questionText: Is your business located at a commercial address in unincorporated St. Lucie County (commercial locations need a Fire Inspection before BTR)?
inferenceHints: Home-based businesses in unincorporated areas don't need the fire inspection. Commercial locations must schedule with SLC Fire District (772-621-3377).

label: Which BTR exemption applies (per Florida Statutes)
questionText: Do you qualify for a BTR exemption (nonprofit 501(c)(3), religious organization, agricultural/farm operation, or veteran fee waiver)?
inferenceHints: Statutory exemptions: §205.192 nonprofit, §205.191 religious, §205.064 agricultural. Veterans have a separate fee-waiver program (not a full exemption).

label: What the customer wants to do with their Tourist Development Tax account
questionText: Are you setting up a new TDT account, filing routine returns, or deactivating your rental account?
inferenceHints: Routine filing is online-only; deactivation uses the Tourist-Inactive form.

label: Whether the property is rented for periods of 6 months or less
questionText: Is your property rented for periods of 6 months or less, or longer?
inferenceHints: TDT applies ONLY to rentals of 6 months or less. Longer-term rentals are not subject to the 5% tourist tax (though state sales tax may still apply).

label: Whether the customer has a Florida Department of Revenue sales-tax ID
questionText: Do you already have a Florida Department of Revenue sales-tax identification number?
inferenceHints: Most TDT registrants need an FDOR sales-tax ID first. Obtain one at floridarevenue.com or by calling 772-429-2900.

label: Whether a property management company files on the owner's behalf
questionText: Do you have a property management company that files returns for you?
inferenceHints: If yes, complete the Tourist Owner-Agent Agreement authorizing the manager to file.

label: Whether the customer already has a TouristExpress account
questionText: Do you already have a TouristExpress account on stlucie.county-taxes.com/tourist?
inferenceHints: New registrations flow through TouristExpress. Customers without an account create one first.

label: What kind of dealer paperwork is being dropped off
questionText: What are you dropping off — a title bundle, reassignment paperwork, temporary-plate stock, towing/storage destruction forms, or closing out your dealership?
inferenceHints: Each category uses different HSMV forms. Title bundle = routine. Out-of-business = cancels the dealer license.

label: Whether the dealer's FLHSMV license is currently active
questionText: Is your Florida motor-vehicle dealer license currently active?
inferenceHints: Expired licenses cannot submit paperwork at the tax collector; customer must renew with FLHSMV Field Operations first.

label: Whether odometer disclosure is captured on the title or needs a separate form
questionText: Is the odometer disclosure already captured on the title, or do you need to include HSMV 82993?
inferenceHints: §319.14 requires disclosure at every transfer for vehicles model-year 2011 or newer. Pre-2011 vehicles are exempt.

label: Which dealer form is being used
questionText: Which HSMV form is this paperwork using — standard title, 82091 reassignment, 83090 temp plate, 82012 towing destruction, or 86060 relinquish license?
inferenceHints: Form type determines which additional checklists/attachments are required.

label: Category of the driver-license sanction
questionText: What type of sanction is on your driver license — unpaid citation, failure to appear/comply, court-ordered school, child-support, points, financial-responsibility (insurance), DUI, habitual traffic offender, drug-offense, medical/vision, or non-DUI serious-injury?
inferenceHints: Each sanction type has a distinct clearance path. Some (failure-to-appear, failure-to-comply, child-support) are NOT eligible for hardship licensing.

valueLabels.non-dui-death-or-serious-injury: Crash with serious injury or death (non-DUI)

label: Current state of the sanction
questionText: Is your license currently under an active suspension/revocation, or has the sanction period expired (but the license is still not reinstated)?
inferenceHints: Expired-but-not-reinstated customers often just need to pay the reinstatement fee. Active suspensions may need course completions or court clearance first.

label: Whether the underlying cause of the sanction has been cleared
questionText: Have you cleared the underlying issue that caused the suspension (paid the citation, satisfied the court, paid child-support, etc.)?
inferenceHints: Court / DOR clearance typically updates FLHSMV electronically. No reinstatement fee can be accepted until the underlying issue is resolved.

label: Whether the required driver-improvement or DUI-program course has been completed
questionText: Have you completed the required course — Advanced Driver Improvement (ADI) or Licensed DUI Program?
inferenceHints: ADI is required for HTO, non-DUI serious-injury, and DUI hardship. Licensed DUI Program is required for DUI and Chapter 893 drug offenses.

valueLabels.na-not-required: Course isn't required for my situation

label: Whether SR-22 insurance is on file with FLHSMV (for financial-responsibility sanctions)
questionText: Is an SR-22 insurance filing on record with FLHSMV (required for financial-responsibility / insurance-related suspensions)?
inferenceHints: SR-22 is filed electronically by your insurance company directly with FLHSMV; the customer doesn't hand-carry a document to the tax collector.

label: Whether an Ignition Interlock Device is required as part of a DUI sanction
questionText: If this is a DUI sanction, is an Ignition Interlock Device (IID) required as part of reinstatement (per §322.2715)?
inferenceHints: IID installation must be performed by an FLHSMV-contracted provider and proof presented at reinstatement.

label: Whether the customer is seeking a hardship license (restricted to employment / business purposes)
questionText: Are you applying for a hardship license (restricted to driving for employment or business purposes only), or full reinstatement?
inferenceHints: Hardship applications go through the Administrative Reviews Office, not the tax collector directly. Failure-to-appear, failure-to-comply, and child-support suspensions are NOT eligible for hardship.

label: What the customer wants to do regarding Tangible Personal Property tax
questionText: Are you trying to pay an existing Tangible Personal Property tax bill, file your TPP return for the year, or asking about the $25,000 exemption?
inferenceHints: Paying a bill = Tax Collector. Filing the return OR applying for exemption = Property Appraiser (paslc.gov). The $25,000 Amendment 1 exemption is claimed via the filed return by April 1 each year.

label: Whether the TPP tax bill is past due (delinquent)
questionText: Is the TPP bill current-year or is it past due (delinquent)?
inferenceHints: Delinquent TPP must be paid with guaranteed funds (cashier's check, cash, debit, credit). Personal checks are rejected on past-due. Customer 'yes' = past due, 'no' = current-year.

label: Vehicle class
questionText: What kind of vehicle is this — a regular passenger car, motorcycle, trailer, low-speed vehicle, vessel, or mobile home?

valueLabels.low-speed-vehicle: Low-speed vehicle (LSV / golf cart with VIN)

label: How the vehicle was constructed
questionText: Was this vehicle made by a manufacturer, built from scratch, assembled from a kit, or rebuilt from salvage?

valueLabels.manufactured: Made by a manufacturer (regular dealer-bought vehicle)

label: Tourist Development Tax filing channel
questionText: How are you filing the Tourist Development Tax — online, in person, or by mail?

valueLabels.in-office: In person at the Tax Collector office

label: Type of entity acquiring title via dealer drop-off
questionText: Is the title being transferred to a Florida-registered business, an out-of-state business, an individual, or a trust?

label: Trailer net weight
questionText: About how much does the trailer weigh empty? Florida treats trailers differently above and below 2,000 lb.

valueLabels.under-2000: Under 2,000 lb (most utility, motorcycle, and small cargo trailers)
valueLabels.2000-or-more: 2,000 lb or more (large cargo, car-hauler, equipment trailers)
valueLabels.unknown: Not sure — I'll bring it to the certified scale before the visit

inferenceHints: Net (empty) weight, not loaded weight. The 2,000-lb cutoff governs whether the trailer must be titled (≥2,000 lb) or is registration-only (<2,000 lb). When unknown, treat as <2,000 lb for the doc list and add a note that the public-scale slip will determine the final classification.

label: How the trailer was built or obtained
questionText: Did you build this trailer yourself, or was it manufactured by a company?

valueLabels.homemade: I built it myself (welded / assembled from parts)
valueLabels.manufactured: It was made by a manufacturer (has a tag / VIN from a company)

inferenceHints: If the customer says DIY, homemade, shop-built, scratch-built, kit-built — record homemade. If they describe a brand, model, or factory tag — manufactured.

label: How the trailer came to the customer
questionText: How did you get the trailer?

valueLabels.private-purchase: Bought it used from a private seller
valueLabels.inherited: Inherited from a family member who passed
valueLabels.out-of-state-transfer: Already registered in another state, moving to Florida

inferenceHints: newly-built and homemade go together. Inherited typically pairs with manufactured. private-purchase implies an existing prior title (if ≥2,000 lb). out-of-state-transfer means the trailer has registration or title in another state being surrendered to FL.

label: Whether the customer can produce material receipts (homemade only)
questionText: For a homemade trailer, Florida calculates 6% sales tax on the cost of materials. Do you have the receipts for the parts you bought?

valueLabels.yes-complete: Yes, I have all my receipts
valueLabels.yes-partial: I have some receipts but not all

inferenceHints: Only relevant for homemade trailers — sales tax is calculated on material cost. Without receipts, the office may estimate from market value or refuse processing.

label: Why the vehicle is being titled into a new owner's name
questionText: What's the reason for this title transfer — did you buy or receive the vehicle from a living owner, or is this because the owner on the title has passed away?
inferenceHints: If the customer mentions a death, inheritance, estate, probate, or that the owner 'passed away'/'died', record inheritance-deceased-owner. A normal purchase, gift, or family transfer between living people is standard-sale-or-gift. This is asked EARLY because an inheritance changes who may legally take title (and must be established before logistics).

valueLabels.standard-sale-or-gift: Bought or received from a living owner
valueLabels.inheritance-deceased-owner: The owner on the title has passed away

label: Whether anyone other than the deceased is named as an owner on the title
questionText: How does the title read — was the deceased the only owner listed, or is there another person named as an owner on the title (for example a spouse)?
inferenceHints: SME-named question (tax423: 'at no point was I asked if there were any additional owners on the title'). surviving-co-owner = another living person is already on the title (often a spouse joined by 'or', so the vehicle usually passes to them directly). sole-owner-deceased = the deceased was the only owner, so the estate determines the heir. na-not-inheritance is an auto-resolved sentinel for non-inheritance transfers. unknown means heirship is not yet established — the transfer is hard-blocked until it is. Ask this EARLY, before title logistics.

valueLabels.surviving-co-owner: Another owner (e.g. spouse) is also on the title
valueLabels.sole-owner-deceased: The deceased was the only owner

label: Whether the deceased owner's estate has a will or probate
questionText: Is there a will, or has the estate gone through (or started) probate?
inferenceHints: SME-named question (tax423: 'also was not asked if there is a will'). will-or-probate = a will exists or the estate is/was in probate (the named representative/heir can act). no-will-no-probate = no will and no probate yet, so the lawful heir is not yet legally established — hard-blocked until resolved. na-surviving-co-owner is auto-resolved when a surviving co-owner is already on the title (the vehicle passes to them, so the will question is moot). na-not-inheritance is the sentinel for non-inheritance transfers.

valueLabels.will-or-probate: Yes — there is a will or probate
valueLabels.na-surviving-co-owner: N/A — a surviving owner is on the title

label: Whether the customer actually has the title and in what form
questionText: Do you have the vehicle's title in hand? Is it a paper title you physically have, an electronic title held by the state, or do you not have it (lost or never received)?
inferenceHints: Asked EARLY so the bot doesn't loop on paper-title-condition questions the customer can't answer (sessions 19d716d3 and ae0b2879, where the customer said up-front they didn't have the title / it was electronic, and the bot re-asked title-condition and paper-type repeatedly). paper-in-hand = normal flow. electronic-held = FLHSMV holds it electronically; no paper to inspect or bring (converted as part of the transfer). lost-or-none = customer lost it or never received it; a duplicate title (HSMV 82101) is needed before/with the transfer. When electronic-held or lost-or-none, the title_condition and title_is_original_paper questions are auto-resolved to na-no-title (no physical title to inspect).

valueLabels.lost-or-none: No — lost it or never had it
